thread:
Ellen Park: Hi folks / quick policy check. I just returned from a 6-week unpaid sabbatical (officially ended Dec 20) and had pre-booked travel for Dec 29-31 to handle post-sabbatical logistics. Those dates fall in the year-end PTO blackout. I have ~4 days of PTO carryover from last year. Any way to preserve those days for the booked travel?
Diego (People Ops): Welcome back, Ellen 94 glad you're back. Sabbaticals have a special reintegration policy but they don't automatically change the year-end blackout rules. That said, we do have a "Sabbatical Reintegration" accommodation that can allow up to 5 days to be exempted from the blackout for the first 30 days after return, provided manager approval and documentation of the sabbatical.
Ellen Park: That would be perfect. My manager Marcus approved the sabbatical before I left. Marcus 94 can you confirm you approve exempting Dec 29-31 as reintegration days?
Marcus Lee: Confirmed 94 I approve the 3 reintegration days and agree they99re business-appropriate. No impact to deliverables.
Diego (People Ops): Process for this accommodation: manager approval in-thread (done), employee attaches sabbatical approval email or HR confirmation to the "Sabbatical Reintegration" form (internal), and People Ops will tag the days as "Reintegration - Bypass Blackout". Payroll will then code them as PTO from carryover. Link: https://intranet.redwood/hr/forms/sabbatical-reintegration (internal).
Ellen Park: Uploaded the sabbatical HR confirmation to the form and attached my manager approval screenshot. Link: https://intranet.redwood/hr/req/SR-2026-55
HR-Bot: Ticket HR-2026-4125 created for Ellen Park (Sabbatical Reintegration) / please attach any additional docs here.
Suki (Payroll): Quick note from payroll: if the carryover balance covers the days we'll post them as "Carryover PTO" and they won't count toward this year's accruals. If carryover is insufficient we can either advance PTO (up to 5 days) or mark unpaid per employee preference. For US-based employees this is regular PTO coding; for EU/APAC please flag local payroll taxes. Processing ETA ~3 business days after docs are in.
Ellen Park: I have 4 carryover days, so this will cover the 3 days. Thanks! Any need to sign an advance agreement?
Diego (People Ops): No advance needed in this case since carryover covers it. One administrative ask: we track these reintegration accommodations for audit so please confirm whether the sabbatical included any training or phased return expectations (just a yes/no).
Ellen Park: Yes / I had a phased return expectation (reduced hours first week).
Nora (Legal): Quick compliance note: please ensure consistent application of reintegration exceptions across regions. People Ops, flag this as "Sabbatical - Return Accommodation" in the audit log and include manager approver and signed sabbatical docs. Also ensure there's no pay/work location change that would trigger cross-border payroll rules.
Marcus Lee: For transparency, Ellen will be at 0.8 FTE for the first two weeks as agreed. I99m fine with the accommodation.
Suki (Payroll): Thanks Marcus / Nora / Diego. Because Ellen is at 0.8 FTE on phased return, payroll will prorate any pay implications if an advance had been used; in this case carryover covers it so no proration needed for the posted days. We99ll post the carryover PTO for Dec 29-31 and update Ellen's accrual ledger.
HR-Bot: HR-2026-4125 updated / People Ops flagged as "Approved - Reintegration" and notified Payroll.
Diego (People Ops): All set on our side once payroll posts. Ellen / payroll will notify when posted. Welcome back again! :tada:
Ellen Park: Thanks so much everyone / really appreciate the quick turnaround.
Suki (Payroll): Posted the carryover PTO for Dec 29-31 / you should see the update on your accruals within 1 business day. Ticket closed unless anyone needs follow-up.
Ellen Park: I see it / all looks good. Thanks team. :heart:
